blogs.title: CROSS-BORDER TOURS
blogs.excerpt: Discover one of Europe’s most unique cycling experiences with a cross-border e-bike ride from Strasbourg into Germany through scenic Rhine routes and historic landscapes.
blogs.content:
Ride Into Germany: Cross-Border E-Bike Tours from Strasbourg

Strasbourg is a city shaped by borders, culture, and movement.

Located along the Rhine River, it offers something unusual—a cycling experience that lets you travel between two countries in a single morning.

Cross the river from Strasbourg and within minutes you arrive in Germany, opening the door to scenic landscapes, riverside paths, and a completely different pace of travel.

The Border That Almost Disappeared

For much of the twentieth century, the French-German border represented separation.

Today, crossing feels almost effortless.

Ride across:

  • Pont de l'Europe

  • Passerelle des Deux Rives

And move from France into Germany in minutes.

No long delays. No complicated transfers. Just continuous movement across one of Europe’s most symbolic regions.

This route offers more than cycling—it gives perspective on how landscapes and cultures connect.

What Awaits on the German Side

Kehl

Only a short ride from Strasbourg, Kehl offers a quieter atmosphere and local experiences.

Things to enjoy:

  • Weekly markets

  • German bakeries

  • Local cafés

  • Relaxed riverside streets

Kehl becomes the perfect first stop before continuing deeper into the route.

Rhine Cycle Path (EuroVelo 15)

One of Europe’s most recognised long-distance cycling routes.

Highlights include:

  • Smooth riding surfaces

  • Riverside scenery

  • Nature reserves

  • Forest landscapes

  • Cross-river viewpoints

The route remains largely flat, making it ideal for e-bike riders of all experience levels.

Rastatt & Baden Wine Villages

Continue north and discover a different side of Germany.

This section introduces:

  • Traditional villages

  • Wine-growing landscapes

  • Black Forest surroundings

  • Scenic detours

Compared with the French side of Alsace, these routes feel quieter and less explored while remaining equally rewarding.

The Practical Side of a Cross-Border Ride

Typical route distance:

25–30 kilometres round trip

An e-bike transforms the experience:

  • Comfortable riding

  • Longer exploration time

  • Easy return journey

  • Flexible stops throughout the route

Since the terrain stays mostly flat, extending your ride becomes simple without adding significant difficulty.

Travellers can comfortably complete the experience as a half-day activity.

Explore with VeloRouge

VeloRouge’s guided cross-border rides combine:

  • Scenic cycling

  • Historical context

  • Local insights

  • Carefully selected routes

Experiences highlight the Rhine landscape, bridge architecture, and the unique cultural identity shared across this region.

Two Countries, One Morning

Few travel experiences let you cross a national border so naturally.

This route reflects what makes Strasbourg special—movement, openness, and connection.

An e-bike gives you enough range to experience both sides properly while still travelling slowly enough to appreciate every detail.

blogs.title: WINE ROUTE CYCLING
blogs.excerpt: Discover the Alsace Wine Route by e-bike and explore vineyard landscapes, medieval villages, and unforgettable cycling experiences across one of France’s most scenic regions.
blogs.content:
The Alsace Wine Route by E-Bike: What the Road Actually Looks Like

The Alsace Wine Route is one of France’s most iconic travel experiences.

Stretching approximately 170 kilometres between Marlenheim and Thann, this route passes through more than 70 wine-producing villages, historic streets, vineyard landscapes, and some of the most picturesque countryside in Europe.

Nobody rides the entire route in a single day—and that is exactly the point.

Exploring sections of it slowly by e-bike gives travellers a more immersive way to experience Alsace.

Why an E-Bike Makes the Wine Route Better

The wine route follows the foothills of the Vosges Mountains.

As you ride:

  • Vineyards rise across the slopes

  • Open countryside stretches toward the Rhine

  • Villages appear one after another

  • Scenic viewpoints become part of the journey

Although the terrain stays manageable, there are gentle climbs throughout the route.

An e-bike allows riders to enjoy the landscape without turning every hill into a challenge.

You choose where to pedal harder and where to enjoy electric assistance—arriving relaxed and ready to enjoy each stop.

The Best Sections to Ride from Strasbourg

Obernai → Barr

One of the most rewarding stretches for a day ride.

Highlights include:

  • Medieval village atmosphere

  • Historic market squares

  • Traditional Alsatian architecture

  • Regional wine experiences

The route covers around 15 kilometres and introduces riders to the southern edge of Bas-Rhin wine country.

Wine lovers can explore local varieties including Riesling and Sylvaner.

Ribeauville → Riquewihr

A shorter ride with maximum scenery.

This section includes:

  • Castle views

  • Historic streets

  • Vineyard landscapes

  • Traditional wine experiences

Covering approximately 5 kilometres, this route offers a relaxed afternoon through one of Alsace’s most photographed areas.

Colmar as Your Riding Base

Located near the centre of the wine route, Colmar works perfectly for day rides.

Before cycling, visitors can enjoy:

  • Historic neighbourhoods

  • Museum visits

  • Canal areas

  • Local cafés and bakeries

Then continue directly into the vineyard landscapes surrounding the city.

Tasting, Stopping, and Riding On

The beauty of cycling the wine route comes from its pace.

Distances between villages often stay short:

  • 3 km

  • 5 km

  • 8 km

Every stop introduces something different:

  • Vineyard visits

  • Traditional restaurants

  • Local bakeries

  • Scenic viewpoints

E-bike travel means enjoying these moments without worrying about the return ride.

  • Scenic riding

The focus is not simply reaching destinations—it is enjoying everything between them.

What to Know Before You Go

Best riding period:

May → October

For an even more memorable experience:

September → October
Harvest season transforms the vineyards into shades of gold and many villages host local harvest celebrations.

blogs.title: FAMILY RIDES
blogs.excerpt: Planning a family trip to Strasbourg? Discover why e-bike rides are one of the easiest and most enjoyable ways to explore the city with children.
blogs.content:
Strasbourg with Kids: Why an E-Bike Ride Works Better Than You Think

Travelling with children means balancing energy, comfort, and keeping everyone engaged throughout the day.

One moment they want to explore everything, and the next they need a break. Strasbourg makes family travel easier—and an e-bike makes it even better.

With safe infrastructure, flat routes, and scenic places to stop, families can enjoy the city without turning sightseeing into a tiring experience.

Flat, Safe, and Designed for Families

Strasbourg has built one of France’s strongest cycling networks.

With more than 600 kilometres of bike lanes—many separated from road traffic—families can ride comfortably and confidently.

The city remains mostly flat, removing the challenge of steep climbs and allowing children to enjoy longer rides without becoming exhausted.

E-bikes reduce the effort for parents and keep the experience relaxed.

Routes That Work Well with Children

Parc de l'Orangerie

One of Strasbourg’s most family-friendly places.

Highlights include:

  • Open green areas

  • Smooth cycling routes

  • Boating lake

  • Small zoo

  • Storks nesting throughout the park

A relaxed morning ride through the park and surrounding canal paths creates an ideal family outing.

La Petite France & Covered Bridges

This historic district remains one of Strasbourg’s most memorable places for children and adults.

Ride slowly through:

  • Canal-side streets

  • Historic bridges

  • Scenic viewpoints

  • Barrage Vauban

Morning visits provide a quieter and more enjoyable experience.

Canal Paths North of Strasbourg

Families wanting a longer ride can explore the quieter canal routes outside the city.

These routes offer:

  • Peaceful surroundings

  • Village scenery

  • Flat riding conditions

  • Comfortable half-day experiences

Perfect for families who want to combine exploration with relaxation.

Why E-Bikes Work Better for Family Travel

Standard bicycles work differently once children join the ride.

Whether using:

  • Cargo bikes

  • Child attachments

  • Independent riding for older kids

Parents usually end up carrying most of the effort.

E-bikes balance the experience.

Parents stay comfortable, children maintain energy, and the ride remains enjoyable from start to finish. Nobody wants to end a family day searching for a taxi halfway through the route.

Family-Friendly Riding with VeloRouge

VeloRouge provides e-bike experiences tailored for family travel.

Routes are selected based on:

  • Comfortable distances

  • Child-friendly pacing

  • Scenic stops

  • Flexible ride durations

The goal is simple—help families enjoy Strasbourg together.

When to Go

Best seasons:

Spring
Comfortable temperatures and lower crowds.

September
Excellent weather with shaded routes and easier riding conditions.

Summer holidays also work well, while August weekends in central areas can become crowded. A relaxed family ride usually lasts between two and three hours with stops.
